explanation: Use two pointers on the already sorted array. Increase the left pointer when the sum is too small and decrease the right pointer when it is too large. Allow the pointers to coincide because this EPI contract permits reusing one element.
timeComplexity: O(n+1) worst-case time for n entries: each unsuccessful comparison discards one endpoint, giving at most n iterations.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: two indices and one sum; the input is not copied or changed.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract; EPI problem attribution remains in the collection.
correctness: At each step all pairs not yet excluded have both indices within the active sorted interval. If the endpoint sum is below target, pairing its left value with any remaining value is also too small; excluding that left endpoint is safe. If it is above target, every remaining pair using the right endpoint is too large. Equality proves a valid pair. Each unsuccessful step shrinks the interval, so exhaustion proves no pair exists. A single remaining index must still be tested because reuse is allowed.
walkthrough: For sorted [-8, 1, 6, 13] and target 12, begin with -8 + 13 = 5 and advance left. Next 1 + 13 = 14, so move right to 6. Then 1 + 6 = 7, so move left to that same 6. Now 6 + 6 = 12; reusing the element is allowed, so return true.
edgeCases: [3] and target 6 return true by reusing its only index.
Repeated values and negative values obey the same sorted-order argument.
Casting before addition evaluates the sum in signed 64-bit arithmetic.
